pages.scan: I opened works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/review/page-04.png with Read and looked at the image itself. It was readable. It has 4 panels with no numbers or guide lines: a full-width top tier, a middle row of two panels (left and right), and a full-width bottom tier. Before looking at the image I read only the request JSON. I did not read the source text, script, workflow, storyboard, reading-flow files or earlier responses.
pages.observation: Natural reading order: (1) top tier, a female doctor (white coat, stethoscope, teal top, hair in a bun) at the desk on the left, Ravi seated on the right: 'Hello, Ravi. Tell me what brings you in.' (2) middle-left, Ravi with his hand on his neck, the doctor's back in the left foreground: 'I've been feeling tired lately.' (3) middle-right, a reverse shot of the doctor listening with her hands folded, Ravi's back on the right, under a rectangular caption box: 'Technology supports the workflow. The conversation stays human.' (4) bottom tier, the doctor gestures: 'We'll go through your concerns and decide the right next steps together.' The order is clear. Tails: P1 the tail points left to the doctor's mouth, correct. P2 the tail reaches Ravi's face, correct. P4 the tail points left to the doctor's mouth and clearly does not mark Ravi. P3 is a caption with no tail. Coverage: no balloon or caption covers a face, hand, stethoscope or bag. The P3 caption's right edge comes very close to the top of Ravi's back-of-head at the panel's right edge, so please check it at 100%. The P4 balloon sits close to the left side of Ravi's head but does not touch his face. Issues to consider: (a) The P3 caption is an abstract narrator theme statement that falls between Ravi's complaint and the doctor's reply. No technology is visible in that panel (only a closed laptop), so the line feels detached from the image and delays her answer. Consider whether it belongs on this page or panel. (b) The doctor's reply in P4 is generic and does not engage with 'tired' (no follow-up question). This is acceptable but slightly disconnected as dialogue. (c) The jump from page 3 ('Please have a seat' in the waiting area) to the consulting room has no transition cue. The setting change reads from the background and the doctor's coat, so it is understandable. The doctor is clearly a different woman from the receptionist (bun and white coat versus braid and blue kurta). The bag stays on the floor to Ravi's right in P1 and P4, which is consistent. Not blocking.
